newsitem.title: USA: INSIGHT - Weak mark propels dollar to new heights.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Weak mark propels dollar to new heights.

text.p: The dollar continued to charge toward highs not seen since February 1994 as the stumbling mark endured significant losses on several charts.
The greenback came within a whisker of a key objective at 1.7405 marks before succumbing to profit-taking on Tuesday and chartists said it should make a serious run at that level in the near future.

"There are potential divergences forming on the hourly charts, so we may see a test of support near 1.73 before we retest the upside. But we remain generally bullish at this point," said Pete Grant, senior analyst at MMS International.

Chartists noted 1.7405 marks represented a short-term peak as the dollar began a descent from 1.7686 in February 1994. After bottoming near 1.70, dollar/mark could get no higher than 1.7405 that month and has never traded that high since.
"That was the extent of the bounce. After the initial drop from (1.7686) ended, dollar/mark died at 1.7405," noted Darren Spain, global forex analyst at Credit Suisse First Boston.

Ironically, 1.7405 marks also offers a more current techical hurdle, Spain noted. That level represents an eight pfenning rise from the late March low at 1.6610, which would match an August to October rally to 1.5455 marks from 1.4645.
"We're looking for an equilibrium move, where the initial upleg of this rally will equal the last upleg," Spain said.
The mark also slumped below 73 yen for the first time in two weeks and nearly equalled its weakest showing in 55 months against the British pound.
"Mark/yen's inability to sustain gains above 74 suggests the highs of 75.33 in January and 75.87 last October are well protected at this point," said Grant.
Furthermore, sterling/mark's prolonged rally leaves open the possibility of a 3.00 reading in coming weeks, so long as it gets past key resistance at 2.8250, Grant added.
"I don't think it (the sterling/mark rally) is over yet," said Grant. "We came within striking distance of that (2.8250) high today, and if we take it out, the long-term objective is 3.00."
Dollar/yen remains tightly rangebound between the 126 area and 126.60, chartists said.
While the long-term trend for dollar/yen still appears bullish, technicians said they would not rule out near-term corrective selling to below 126.
